response.answer: BV uncertainty bounds adjust RCV and flag rates for K+, creatinine, and troponin by providing tighter individual reference intervals, reducing false positives and negatives. Conflicting BV sources are resolved by prioritizing the most recent, peer-reviewed data.

results.title: Biological variation and reference (normal) values
results.content: Test results are commonly interpreted against population-based reference (normal) intervals, which should be provided on every laboratory report, irrespective of whether the test has been done as point-of-care testing or in a clinical laboratory. In consequence, individuals can have results that are highly unusual for them but still lie within reference intervals, making clinical laboratory tests poor in diagnosis and for screening. Individuals can have results that vary over time within and outside reference intervals, often causing clinical confusion. The Registrar said that this was a nice theoretical concept but there were very many tests done in laboratory medicine both as POCT and in laboratories and asked how the reference intervals supplied with each report for every test done were obtained in practice. The Clinical Biochemist referred to a previous ward round at which the concepts of within-subject and between-subject biological variation had been discussed [2]. The Charge Nurse at the round remarked that neither the POCT analyzer nor most laboratory reports would flag such results because the individual's results were simply compared to the population reference interval and this very real “abnormality” would be missed. However, changes in creatinine were very useful indicators of real changes in renal function, and the Registrar remarked that the use of reference change values (RCV), discussed at an earlier ward round [2], obviously had significant advantages over population-based reference intervals in monitoring change in individual patients. The Registrar remarked that it was also interesting that individuals could have results that changed, simply through inherent variation, from within to outside reference intervals. The Registrar then stated that the reference intervals for creatinine on both the POCT analyzer and the laboratory reports were not always the same. The first was that clinicians should really only use the reference intervals provided on the POCT analyzer or by the laboratory that produced the test results, and that was a major reason why reference intervals were included on every report. If urine creatinine output was taken as an example, for men and women together as one population group, the index of individuality is 0.46 and therefore a single population-based reference interval would be of little value – exactly as per the scenario for serum creatinine.

Biological variation and reference change value of the estimated glomerular filtration rate in humans: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Biological variation and reference change value of the estimated glomerular filtration rate in humans: A systematic review and meta-analysis. **Background:** Knowledge of the biological variation of serum or plasma creatinine (Cr) and the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is important for understanding disease dynamics in Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD). **Methods:** We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on biological variation of Cr. Relevant studies were identified by systematic literature search on PubMed. Additional studies were retrieved from the European Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (EFLM) Biological Variation Database. **Keywords:** CKD progression; biological variation; chronic kidney disease; estimated glomerular filtration rate; reference change value (RCV). results.title: Biological variation: recent development and future chall...
results.content: Biological variation (BV) data have many applications in laboratory medicine. These range from new models and approaches to derive BV data, the delivery of high-quality BV data by the highly powered European Biological Variation Study (EuBIVAS), the Biological Variation Data Critical Appraisal Checklist (BIVAC) and other standards for deriving and reporting BV data, the EFLM Biological Variation Database and new applications of BV data including personalized reference intervals and measurement uncertainty. 2. Delivery of high-quality BV data from the highly powered European Biological Variation Study (EuBIVAS). ## Delivery of high-quality BV estimates – the European Biological Variation Study (EuBIVAS). EuBIVAS has so far delivered BV estimates for 81 different measurands; with data for two target measurands (cardiac troponin and serum creatinine) obtained using two different analytical methods [20: weekly biological variation of cardiac troponin I estimated by the use of two different high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I assays. The result of this work was, among others, the Biological Variation Data Critical Appraisal Checklist (BIVAC), a standard for evaluating BV studies [25]. The BIVAC also provides, in combination with the Biological Variation Data Reporting Checklist [26], a framework that may help those planning BV studies both to perform and publish their study in an appropriate manner. The “EFLM Biological Variation Database” was launched during the EuroMedLab in Barcelona in May 2019 and is available at To populate the database, systematic literature searches for BV studies for relevant measurands have been performed and identified publications appraised by the BIVAC. In this database, detailed information for biological variation data sets derived from critically appraised biological variation studies, as well global CVI and CVG from meta-analysis are published and automatically updated whenever new data are added. The results of many of these initiatives have been incorporated in the EFLM Biological Variation Database, which provides quality-assessed BV data, with automatically calculated BV applications, freely available for users worldwide. .Search in Google Scholar PubMed. results.title: Reference change values based on uncertainty models - ScienceDirect
results.content: Nevertheless, we propose two uncertainty-based models to estimate reference change values which will include all possible variation sources. ### Methods The models consisted in 1) estimation of the uncertainty related to each measured value, 2) calculation of the change between these values and its uncertainty, and 3) performing a compatibility study to know if the values are of the same degree of equivalence. The Harris' approach assumes that measured values of a quantity and the changes between two measured values are normally distributed, and the standard ANOVA method is used to estimate the within-subject biological coefficient of variation () [4]. Keeping in mind the essence of the RCV approaches mentioned above, we propose two different models to estimate RCV using the uncertainty, biological variation, and compatibility concepts, which could implement in clinical laboratories.
